content:
Samuel Achterberg-Osei
Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Engineer

[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LOCATION] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing and operating Azure environments, building infrastructure as code with Terraform, and delivering deployment automation through Azure DevOps. Experience includes Azure landing-zone networking, AKS operations, cloud migration, and security automation. Combines systems administration experience across Windows and Linux with practical infrastructure automation using PowerShell.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: Microsoft Azure, Azure IaaS, Azure landing zones, Azure Migrate, Azure VMs
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Terraform modules, PowerShell, Azure DevOps YAML pipelines, Go (Terratest tests), Python (small scripts)
Networking and security: Hub-spoke networking, VNets, VNet peering, Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints, site-to-site VPN, Microsoft 365 security baselines, Entra ID, MFA, conditional access
Containers and delivery: AKS operations (upgrades, node pools, ingress), Docker, Helm, App Service, CI/CD
Systems: Windows and Linux servers, VMware, Proxmox

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics | 2025–Present
- Build and maintain Azure landing-zone infrastructure, Terraform modules, Azure DevOps pipelines, and AKS environments.
- Designed a hub-spoke network in Terraform, including Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering across three subscriptions.
- Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and a nightly infrastructure drift-detection job.
- Replaced manual deployment processes for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines for build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS.
- Helped increase deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.
- Operate AKS upgrades, node pools, and ingress; application manifests are managed by developers.

Freelance IT Support | 2022–2023
- Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for small-business Microsoft 365 security baselines.
- Enabled MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing, and backups for small clients.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services | 2014–2020
- Administered Windows and Linux servers and supported IT services in a municipal environment.
- Planned and executed the lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate.
- Completed cut-over over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.
- Used PowerShell to automate infrastructure and administrative tasks.

CAREER BREAKS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT

Caregiving and unpaid IT support | Mar 2020–Aug 2022
- Left municipal employment to provide full-time care for father; provided unpaid IT help to church and family during this period.

Independent study and cloud training | Feb 2024–Feb 2025
- Studied Terraform and built a Proxmox homelab.
- Completed a three-month, part-time online, English-language cloud bootcamp in Dec 2024.

CERTIFICATIONS
- Azure Administrator Associate
- Terraform Associate, 2025

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with a clear target title, relevant Azure/Terraform/DevOps experience, quantified infrastructure and deployment achievements, and transparent treatment of career breaks. The strongest evidence is the Azure landing-zone networking work, the migration of 60 servers without unplanned downtime, and the automation of deployments for 15 applications. The main content weakness is that some valuable scale and responsibility details from the original candidate information are omitted, particularly administration of approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers and support for municipal services. The document also does not demonstrate several role-specific requirements, such as Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS, stakeholder leadership, or IoT/remote-device integration; these are candidate-experience gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The single-column structure, standard section headings, plain-text bullets, and conventional chronology should parse well in most ATS platforms. Keyword coverage is strong for Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, AKS, networking, security, Linux, Windows, VMware, and virtual machines. AI screening probability is good for Azure-focused cloud infrastructure and DevOps roles, but only moderate for this specific vacancy because the CV does not contain supported evidence for Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, technical leadership/stakeholder alignment, or AWS. The [EMAIL], [PHONE], [LOCATION], and [LINKEDIN] placeholders should not remain in a submitted version because they may reduce recruiter usability and contact-data parsing.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV shows hands-on infrastructure engineering and cloud environment design and operation through Azure landing zones, hub-spoke networking, Terraform modules, Azure DevOps pipelines, AKS operations, and Azure migration. It also shows practical security awareness through Azure Firewall, private endpoints, Entra ID, MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing, and Microsoft 365 security baselines. Terraform is strongly evidenced, although Terragrunt is not. The candidate's systems administration, Linux, Windows, VMware, Proxmox, and Azure VM background aligns with the nice-to-have systems requirements. The material does not show AWS, IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, mTLS or SSL/TLS, backend/full-stack development, or experience leading technical proposals and bringing stakeholders along. The CV demonstrates design and delivery ownership, but it does not explicitly evidence the communication and stakeholder-leadership dimension of the role.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE CV CHANGES:
1. In the contact header, replace [EMAIL], [PHONE], [LOCATION], and [LINKEDIN] with the candidate's actual professional contact details and LinkedIn URL before submitting. Keep the information in plain text rather than icons or images so it remains ATS-readable.
2. In the Systems Administrator entry under Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, add the supported scale and service context from the original candidate information. For example, revise the first bullet to: "Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers and supported staff across several municipal services." This adds credible scale and improves alignment with infrastructure-operation requirements.
3. In the Professional Summary, make the existing architecture and operation evidence more explicit without adding unsupported technologies. For example, change the opening to: "Cloud infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing, building, and operating Azure environments, including landing-zone network architecture, Terraform infrastructure as code, Azure DevOps deployment automation, and AKS operations." This uses the job's terminology while remaining supported by the experience section.
4. In the Core Skills section, retain "Terraform" and "Terraform modules" but do not add "Terragrunt," mTLS, SSL/TLS, AWS, IoT, or certificate management unless the candidate can substantiate those capabilities. The current CV should present a truthful Azure/Terraform profile rather than attempt to match unsupported keywords.

MINOR / TARGETED ENHANCEMENTS:
5. In the Cloud Engineer entry, revise the hub-spoke bullet to emphasize system and network design while staying factual: "Designed and implemented hub-spoke cloud network architecture in Terraform, including Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering across three subscriptions." This makes the existing systems-design evidence easier for ATS and recruiters to identify.
6. In the Cloud Engineer entry, preserve the scope boundary in the AKS bullet but make operational ownership clearer: "Operate AKS upgrades, node pools, and ingress; application manifests remain owned by development teams." This presents accurate platform responsibility without implying application-development ownership.
7. In the Certifications section, use the full certification name consistently, for example "Microsoft Azure Administrator Associate" and "HashiCorp Terraform Associate, 2025," only if those names accurately reflect the certificates held. Do not add certification codes or dates that are not confirmed in the candidate information.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- “Build and maintain ... AKS environments” — the candidate’s material supports operating AKS, including upgrades, node pools and ingress, but does not explicitly support building or maintaining AKS environments.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional, well-structured CV with clear sections, relevant technologies, quantified scope, and credible achievement statements. The strongest evidence is the Azure landing-zone work, Terraform modules, Azure DevOps automation, AKS operations, and the migration of 60 servers with no unplanned downtime. The career breaks are explained transparently and professionally. The main content weakness is that several role-relevant capabilities are implied rather than explicitly framed in the job ad's language, particularly systems architecture/system design and technical leadership. The CV also contains contact placeholders, so it is not submission-ready in its current form.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional headings, plain text, standard bullet points, readable date formatting, and no tables, graphics, columns, or unusual symbols. It contains strong keywords for Azure infrastructure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, networking, AKS, security, Linux, Windows, and virtual machines. AI screening probability is good for Azure-focused Cloud Infrastructure or DevOps roles, but only moderate for this specific vacancy because Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, AWS, IoT/remote-device integration, and technical stakeholder leadership are not evidenced. Do not add those terms unless supported by actual experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with hands-on infrastructure engineering, Azure cloud design and operation, Terraform, networking, practical security, Linux, virtual machines, and operational reliability. The three-subscription hub-spoke architecture, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, private DNS, VPN, AKS operations, drift detection, and deployment automation are particularly relevant to the platform-infrastructure scope. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background even though AWS is preferred. The candidate's material does not establish Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, JVM/backend development, or experience leading technical proposals and bringing external stakeholders along; these are genuine alignment gaps rather than defects that can be solved through wording. The CV does not currently provide direct evidence of the company's collaborative or ownership-oriented culture, but unsupported cultural claims should not be added.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL
1. In the contact header, replace "[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LOCATION] | [LINKEDIN]" with the candidate's real professional contact details and LinkedIn URL. This is necessary for the CV to be usable by a recruiter and parsed as a complete application document.

TARGETED ENHANCEMENTS
2. In the Professional Summary, revise the opening to use the vacancy's terminology while staying truthful. For example: "Cloud infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing, building, and operating Azure cloud environments and infrastructure as code. Experience includes systems architecture for Azure landing zones, Terraform module development, Azure DevOps deployment automation, AKS operations, cloud migration, networking, and practical security automation." Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, AWS, or IoT.

3. In the Cloud Engineer experience section under Havenstad Logistics, revise the first bullet from "Build and maintain Azure landing-zone infrastructure, Terraform modules, and Azure DevOps pipelines" to "Build and operate Azure landing-zone infrastructure, Terraform modules, and Azure DevOps deployment pipelines." This more directly mirrors the requirement for cloud environment design and operation without overstating the role.

4. In the Havenstad Logistics section, make the systems-architecture evidence more explicit by revising the hub-spoke bullet to begin: "Designed and implemented the Azure landing-zone network architecture in Terraform..." Retain the existing details about Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints, VNet peering, and three subscriptions.

5. In the Havenstad Logistics section, clarify the boundary of AKS responsibility while making the operational ownership easier to scan: "Operate AKS upgrades, node pools, and ingress; development teams own application manifests." This is already truthful and avoids implying unsupported application-platform ownership.

6. In the Systems Administrator section, revise "Planned and executed the lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate" to "Planned and executed the Azure IaaS migration of 60 Windows and Linux servers from VMware using Azure Migrate; completed cut-over over six weekends with no unplanned downtime." This connects the achievement more directly to systems architecture, virtual machines, and reliable operations.

7. In the Skills section, add the supported phrase "cloud environment design and operation" under "Cloud and infrastructure" or "Systems," and add "systems architecture" only where it describes the documented Azure landing-zone and migration work. Do not list "system design" as an independent skill unless the experience bullets substantiate it.

8. Check the date presentation for internal consistency. The document shows "Freelance IT Support | 2022–2023" alongside a caregiving period ending in August 2022. Either use precise months where known or clarify that the freelance work began after the caregiving period; do not change dates without verifying them from the candidate's records.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional, and easy to scan. It presents credible Azure, Terraform, networking, migration, CI/CD, AKS, and systems-administration experience with useful scale and outcome metrics: 250 servers, 60-server migration, 15 applications, three subscriptions, and increased deployment frequency. The career-break section is transparent and appropriately explains the timeline. The main content weakness is that several role-critical capabilities are either absent or not explicitly evidenced: Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS, system-design decision-making, technical leadership, and stakeholder alignment. Some wording could also be more precise—for example, the summary says “security automation,” while the evidence is specifically Microsoft 365 security-baseline automation.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses standard headings, reverse-chronological experience, readable bullets, and ATS-friendly plain-text terminology. It contains strong matching keywords such as Azure, Terraform, infrastructure as code, landing zones, hub-spoke networking, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, AKS, Docker, Helm, CI/CD, Linux, VMware, and Azure Migrate. AI/ATS screening probability is good for Azure infrastructure and DevOps roles, but only moderate for this specific vacancy because the CV does not contain supported evidence for Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, stakeholder leadership, or system-design leadership. “Microsoft 365 security baselines” is less directly relevant to the advertised fleet-connectivity platform than the networking and infrastructure content. The formatting is parsing-friendly; no tables, graphics, columns, or unusual section names are present.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with hands-on infrastructure engineering, Azure environment design and operation, Terraform, networking, practical security, Linux, and virtual machines. The Azure landing-zone project and VMware-to-Azure migration are particularly relevant evidence of designing and operating production infrastructure. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background because the advertisement states that AWS is preferred but other major clouds are acceptable. The profile is less aligned with the role’s fleet-connectivity scope: the candidate material does not show AWS, Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, backend or JVM development, or explicit experience leading technical proposals and bringing stakeholders along. The CV also does not explicitly demonstrate observability, certificate management, telemetry, or train-to-cloud interfaces. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be repaired through wording. The document shows a collaborative delivery context indirectly through application-team pipelines, but it does not provide direct evidence of stakeholder leadership.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the broad phrase “security automation” with the more precise supported wording “Microsoft 365 security-baseline automation, including MFA, conditional access, mailbox auditing, and backups.” This avoids overstating the security scope and makes the evidence more credible.
2. In the Professional Experience section under Havenstad Logistics, make the architecture and systems-design contribution more explicit without claiming unsupported ownership. Change “Designed and implemented hub-spoke cloud network architecture in Terraform...” to “Designed and implemented a hub-spoke Azure network architecture in Terraform across three subscriptions, including Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for Storage and SQL, and VNet peering.”
3. In the Havenstad Logistics section, make the cross-team delivery context clearer using only the evidence already present. Change “Replaced manual deployment processes for 15 internal .NET and Node applications...” to “Replaced manual deployment processes for 15 internal .NET and Node applications by creating Azure DevOps YAML CI/CD pipelines for build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS, supporting development teams whose application manifests remained under their ownership.” This better supports the role’s requirement to work with backend developers and agree responsibilities, without claiming formal stakeholder leadership.
4. In the Core Skills section, separate directly demonstrated skills from narrower tools. Change “Go (Terratest tests)” to “Go (Terratest infrastructure tests only)” and change “Python (small scripts)” to “Python (small scripts; not application development).” This accurately reflects the candidate notes and prevents overinterpretation by recruiters or AI screening systems.
5. In the Professional Experience section under Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, strengthen the migration bullet with the supported leadership wording from the original candidate material. Change “Planned and executed the lift-and-shift migration...” to “Led the planning and execution of a lift-and-shift migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate; completed cut-over over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.”

MINOR ATS / PRESENTATION ENHANCEMENTS
6. In the Core Skills section, use the exact job-relevant phrase “systems architecture” where supported by the documented network-design work. Add a narrowly worded item such as “Systems architecture: Azure landing-zone and hub-spoke network design.” Do not add broad claims of enterprise system-design leadership.
7. In the Core Skills section, expand “CI/CD” to “CI/CD and deployment automation” because the experience specifically shows Azure DevOps YAML pipelines for build, test, and deployment. Keep the existing Azure DevOps wording as well.
8. In the Certifications section, add the certification issuer or standard title only if it is available in the candidate’s records; otherwise retain the current concise entries. Do not add certification dates for Microsoft Azure Administrator Associate when no date is provided.
